key_insight: A DSL-guided multi-agent LLM framework can improve inverse materials design by grounding natural-language rules in symbolic predicates and statistical evidence.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a practical path to faster, more interpretable discovery of candidate materials for energy-related applications without requiring large task-specific training datasets.
method: Translate design rules from natural language into chemistry DSL predicates.
Let agents query accumulated materials data to validate, refute, and refine rules during iterative search.
Use ORCHESTRA to run multi-agent inverse design for double perovskite oxides under multiple target-property objectives.
evidence_signal: Compared with natural-language-only rules, the DSL-guided framework improved design performance in the abstract, especially for challenging target properties, by helping the agent identify unsupported rules and update the rule store.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the DSL rules and underlying materials data, so sparse or biased evidence could limit reliability.
paper_title: Symbolic Predicate-Guided Language Agents for Inverse Design of Perovskite Oxides
